newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rise on fresh optimism.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rise on fresh optimism.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 3.63 percent on Thursday, building on strong gains since the start of the year, and traders said renewed optimism in the market should continue to drive prices up.
"I think the trend is not just positive but very positive, and I can not see any reason for declines in the near future," said Rolando Krajnik, a trader at brokerage Perspektiva.
The 10-share SBI index rose 44.49 points to close at 1,271.8, bringing its gains since the start of the year to 7.31 percent.
Turnover rose to 345.9 million tolars from 234.0 million tolars. Overall 11 shares rose, eight fell and six were untraded.

Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most actively traded share, rising 8.72 percent to 22,950 tolars on volume of 5,575 shares for total turnover of 125.4 million tolars in what traders described as foreign-led buying.
"Foreign investors continued to buy shares of Lek and food processing companies like Kolinska and Droga," Krajnik added.
Food company Kolinska rose 8.33 percent to 2,275 tolars on volume of 26,498 shares. Its competitor Droga rose 4.26 percent to 24,500 tolars on volume of 501 shares.
Health resort operator Terme Catez was the biggest gainer, jumping 10.09 percent to 13,200 tolars on volume of 4,751 shares for total turnover of 60.6 million tolars.
Brokerage Dadas was the leading decliner, tumbling 12.68 percent to 6,200 tolars on volume of 78 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
